dedupe_keys.name: cepal ciberataques a la logistica y la infraestructura critica en america latina y el caribe 2023 with an inventory of 82 incidents

description: This CEPAL project document reviews cyber attacks on logistics and critical infrastructure in Latin America and the Caribbean and the state of national cybersecurity. Rodrigo Mariano Díaz and Georgina Núñez of the Division of Production, Productivity and Management wrote it in 2023 under a European Union regional facility. Its inventory of 82 incidents records which security properties were affected, availability in 54 cases, confidentiality in 74 and integrity in 25, and it adds monthly event counts reported by national computer security incident response teams, 2022 growth in reports for Buenos Aires, Panama, Chile and Brazil, weekly attack rates by region and the 2020 maturity and legislation of the countries studied, with annex tables for Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Panama, Peru, the Dominican Republic and Uruguay. Coverage is the region, mainly 2020 to 2022. Format and access: a 63-page Spanish PDF from the CEPAL repository. Licence: United Nations copyright; free to read. Caveats: incidents come from public reports and CSIRT replies, so coverage is uneven. It gives a regional threat baseline for hazard exposure and resilience studies of cyber risk to ports, logistics and utilities. A related catalogue record is the Dyadic Cyber Incident Dataset.
